summary: A cardholder with no previous balance makes a purchase that stays within the credit limit, receives a statement, and pays the full statement balance before the due date. This scenario exercises an on-time full-payment path where the minimum payment obligation is satisfied, the grace-period condition is preserved, and neither a late fee nor an over-limit fee should apply.
assumptions: The account begins this billing cycle with no previous balance, so the grace-period condition is satisfied for new purchases.
The credit limit is $1000.00, and the single purchase in this scenario does not cause the outstanding balance to exceed that limit.
The statement for this cycle closes on 2025-05-31 and sets a payment due date of 2025-06-25, providing at least 25 days after statement closing.
The cardholder makes one standard payment that is credited on the date received and clears successfully before the due date.

Although clause.grace_period_obligation is modeled as an obligation, in this on-time full-payment archetype it is treated as satisfied by paying the full statement balance before interest on new purchases would be imposed.
No cash advances, foreign transactions, returned payments, illegal use, or billing disputes occur in this scenario.
